headline: Nvidia unveils open Nemotron for Science model at SC26
dek: The model runs locally and targets labs, per Nvidia.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The launch
body: Nvidia announced Nemotron for Science, an open model for research labs, at SC26, per NVIDIA and SiliconANGLE.
It pairs Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with open chemistry data (NVIDIA).

points.t: Runs on a DGX Spark workstation or a PC.
It does not rely on the company's cloud.
Includes post-training for chemistry, life science.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: Sweden's KTH reported that an agent fixed 81% of broken GROMACS setups in one night (SiliconANGLE).
It all ran on a single DGX Spark workstation (SiliconANGLE).

stat.cap: of broken setups fixed in one night (SiliconANGLE)

caption.hook: Nvidia unveiled Nemotron for Science, an open model built for research labs.
body: Per NVIDIA and SiliconANGLE, the announcement came at SC26 in Chicago. The model combines Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with an open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes, and can run locally, without relying on the company's cloud.

SiliconANGLE reports that Sweden's KTH used an agent built on the model to fix 81% of broken GROMACS setups in one night. Nvidia also presented the Rubin HPC GPU, planned for 2028, and a quantum computing partnership with IBM and Fermilab.
caption.cta: Could open AI models speed up your lab's work?
